findings.title: Stop agents in all active GUI sessions before deleting the system app
findings.explanation: A directory-backed user can log in, start the shared LaunchAgent, and then switch to another user without logging out. Such an account need not appear in dscl . and is no longer the /dev/console owner. The removal script therefore never boots out that user's agent, yet removes the shared app and reports successful removal. The already-running collector can continue collecting and uploading after the administrator has uninstalled it. The same incomplete enumeration also leaves that session on the old process during system upgrades.
findings.evidence: The new script builds its entire stop list from local directory records plus only the current console account (lines 27–35), then unconditionally deletes the app at line 57. renderSystemPlist installs a shared per-login agent, including for directory-backed accounts, and there is no final check for remaining processes or GUI service instances. postInstallSystem/localUsers uses the same local-plus-current-console enumeration. This system-wide lifecycle did not exist in the base.
findings.fix: Enumerate every active GUI login/service instance, including switched-away directory accounts, and stop and verify all matching shipper services before deleting shared files; use the same complete session set for upgrades.

findings.title: Route fatal errors and panic output into the managed agent log
findings.explanation: For a system agent with a malformed local configuration, runLoop returns the startup error, the deferred Close closes the managed log, and main prints the error directly to os.Stderr. Setting Cobra's output/error writers does not redirect os.Stderr. The new shared plist has no StandardErrorPath, so the actual reason for the restart loop is lost from agent.err.log. Top-level panic stacks are lost through the same route. This defeats the documented startup diagnostics precisely when enrollment or collection cannot start.
findings.evidence: Trace: run.go sets only cmd.SetOut/SetErr, runLoop returns app.New errors, and cmd/quesma-shipper/main.go prints returned errors and recovered panic stacks to os.Stderr. renderSystemPlist omits StandardErrorPath, whereas the base per-user renderPlist redirects process stderr to agent.err.log. The startup-failure record is a separate artifact and does not preserve the missing process stderr/panic stack in the documented log.
findings.fix: Keep the managed log alive through top-level error/panic reporting and route those reporters to it, or redirect process stdout/stderr safely when starting the system agent. Add a test covering a fatal startup error under the managed-agent logging path.
